body: Cases: Amazon (~2,500x 1997-2021), Booking (~800x from 2002), MercadoLibre (~130x since IPO), Netflix (~1,000x), Shopify (~100x to 2021), Meta (~9x from trough), Apple 2016-23 (Services toll on installed base), Axon (hardware -> SaaS). Shared mechanics: each additional user/merchant/supplier makes the service more valuable to the others; revenue scales as a take-rate on GMV/bookings/engagement rather than as units; incremental margins are high so EPS lags then explodes. Visible early signals: payments or ads attach rising (Shopify Payments, Mercado Pago TPV outgrowing GMV), a segment growing much faster than the parent (Booking.com inside Priceline, AWS inside Amazon), engagement intact while price collapses (Netflix 2011/2022, Meta 2022). Failure mode: platforms that drift into capital-heavy operations lose their multiple (Shopify logistics 2022) and win it back when they exit (2023 Flexport sale). Platforms still suffer -75% to -94% drawdowns; the edge is distinguishing a broken stock from a broken network.

data.signal: attach/take-rate rising; engagement intact during price crash

title: Platform economics: take-rate on a growing network beats selling units
